issues.description: Class identifier mismatch: the exercise specification and solution use a class named Meal with constructor Meal(String, String[]) and getters, but the template repository provides a class named Order with that constructor and getters while Meal.java in the template is empty. Problem statement: describes and diagrams a Meal class. Template repository: defines Order (package/class at src/de/tum/cit/ase/Order.java) and leaves src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java empty. Solution repository: implements Meal in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java. This inconsistency forces students to either rename Order to Meal or rework provided files, will cause compilation errors with code expecting Meal, and is likely to confuse learners about the required class name and API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template match the problem statement and solution: provide a Meal class in the template with constructor Meal(String, String[]) and getters (populate src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java accordingly). Remove or rename the template's Order class (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Order.java) to avoid duplicate/conflicting types, or update Main and other template references consistently to use Meal. Ensure the package and API (constructor and getters) match the problem statement exactly so students can compile and follow the specification without renaming files.

issues.description: The conceptual entity representing a food item with a name and ingredient list is called 'Meal' in the problem statement and in the solution implementation, but the template repository exposes the same concept under the different identifier 'Order'. Specifically: the problem statement describes a class named Meal (Meal(String, String[])), the template contains src/de/tum/cit/ase/Order.java which defines class Order(String, String[]), and the solution contains src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java. This name mismatch (Meal vs Order) prevents students from directly locating/using the expected Meal type from the starter code and increases cognitive load when mapping requirements to the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent with the problem statement and solution: rename the template's Order class/file to Meal (i.e., change the class declaration to 'public class Meal' and the filename to Meal.java) and update all references (e.g., in Main and any imports) accordingly. Alternatively, add a Meal class in the template that delegates to or wraps the existing Order implementation so that a type named Meal is available to students.
